residencyRequirements.description: The petitioner must be domiciled in Louisiana. Six months of parish residency establishes domicile for filing purposes. The petition is filed in the parish where either party is domiciled.
residencyRequirements.statute: La. C.C. Art. 10; La. C.C.P. Art. 3941

noChildren.description: Under Article 102, the spouses must live separate and apart for 180 days after service of the petition (when there are no minor children).

withChildren.description: Under Article 102, the spouses must live separate and apart for 365 days after service of the petition (when there are minor children of the marriage).

article103.description: Under Article 103, if the spouses have already lived separate and apart for the required period (180 days without children / 365 days with children), divorce may be granted immediately upon proof of separation.

fault.description: No waiting period for fault-based divorce (adultery or felony conviction with death or hard labor sentence).

covenantMarriage.description: Covenant marriage requires 2 years of separation (or applicable fault grounds after mandatory counseling).

waitingPeriod.notes: Louisiana waiting periods depend on the type of divorce filed (Article 102 vs. 103) and whether minor children are involved.

noFault.name: Article 102 No-Fault (File First, Then Wait)
noFault.description: Petition is filed first, then spouses must live separate and apart for 180 days (no children) or 365 days (with children) after service of the petition before divorce is granted.

noFault.name: Article 103 No-Fault (Already Separated)
noFault.description: Spouses have already lived separate and apart for the required period (180 days without children / 365 days with children). Divorce may be granted immediately upon proof.

fault.name: Adultery
fault.description: The other spouse has committed adultery.

fault.name: Felony Conviction
fault.description: The other spouse has been convicted of a felony and has been sentenced to death or imprisonment at hard labor.

covenantMarriage.name: Felony Conviction (Covenant)
covenantMarriage.description: The other spouse has been convicted of a felony and sentenced to death or imprisonment at hard labor.

covenantMarriage.name: Abandonment (Covenant)
covenantMarriage.description: The other spouse has abandoned the matrimonial domicile for one year and constantly refuses to return.

covenantMarriage.name: Physical or Sexual Abuse (Covenant)
covenantMarriage.description: The other spouse has physically or sexually abused the spouse or a child of one of the spouses.

covenantMarriage.name: Two-Year Separation (Covenant)
covenantMarriage.description: The spouses have lived separate and apart for at least two years.

groundsForDissolution.notes: Louisiana is a civil law state. Divorce grounds are codified in the Civil Code (Articles 102-103) and the Revised Statutes. Covenant marriages have additional requirements including mandatory counseling before filing.

propertyDivision.description: Louisiana is a community property state. All property acquired during the marriage (except by gift, inheritance, or by the terms of a prenuptial agreement) is community property and is divided equally (50/50) upon divorce. Each spouse retains their separate property.
propertyDivision.separateProperty: Separate property includes property acquired before the marriage, property acquired during the marriage by gift or inheritance, and property designated as separate by valid matrimonial agreement. Fruits and revenues of separate property are community property unless otherwise provided by matrimonial agreement.
propertyDivision.statute: La. C.C. Art. 2336 et seq.; La. R.S. 9:2801

filingFees.notes: Louisiana filing fees vary by parish. Typically $200-$600. Fee waivers are available for qualifying low-income individuals via an Application for In Forma Pauperis (IFP).

basic.name: Petition for Divorce
basic.description: Initiates the divorce proceeding under Article 102 or Article 103

basic.name: Citation
basic.description: Formal notice to respondent served by sheriff or private process server

basic.name: Affidavit of Domicile
basic.description: Sworn statement establishing domicile in the parish of filing

basic.name: Rule to Show Cause (Article 102)
basic.description: Motion filed after the waiting period to set the divorce hearing — required for Article 102 divorces

basic.name: Judgment of Divorce
basic.description: Final court order dissolving the marriage

service.name: Citation and Service by Sheriff
service.description: Domiciliary service by the parish sheriff — standard service method in Louisiana

service.name: Waiver of Citation and Service
service.notes: Must be signed by respondent before a notary public

withChildren.name: Custody Implementation Plan
withChildren.description: Joint custody implementation order designating domiciliary and non-domiciliary parent per La. R.S. 9:335

withChildren.name: Child Support Obligation Worksheet
withChildren.description: Calculation per Louisiana Child Support Guidelines (La. R.S. 9:315 et seq.)

withChildren.name: Child Support Order
withChildren.description: Court order establishing child support obligations

formattingRequirements.notes: Per Louisiana District Court local rules

inState.description: Respondent must file a response within 15 days of service (La. C.C.P. Art. 1001)

outOfState.description: Respondent served outside Louisiana has 15 days from service plus additional time for long-arm service

childSupportGuidelines.description: Louisiana uses an income shares model. Both parents' gross incomes are combined and the child support obligation is determined from the Louisiana Child Support Guidelines schedule based on combined adjusted gross income and the number of children.
childSupportGuidelines.notes: The court may deviate from the guidelines if application would not be in the best interest of the child or would be inequitable to the parties.

maintenanceGuidelines.description: Louisiana provides for two types of spousal support: (1) Interim spousal support — awarded during the divorce proceeding based on the needs of the claimant and the ability of the other spouse to pay, considering the standard of living during the marriage; (2) Final periodic support — awarded after divorce to a spouse who is free from fault and lacks sufficient means for support, limited to one-third of the obligor's net income and subject to modification.
maintenanceGuidelines.eligibility: Interim support: based on need and ability to pay. Final periodic support: claimant must be free from fault in the breakup of the marriage and must lack sufficient means for support.
maintenanceGuidelines.statute: La. C.C. Art. 111 (interim); La. C.C. Art. 112-113 (final periodic)

court.name: District Court
court.description: Divorce is filed in the District Court of the parish where either party is domiciled. Louisiana courts are organized by judicial district and parish, not by county.

notes: Louisiana is the only U.S. civil law state. Its legal system derives from the French Napoleonic Code. Louisiana uses PARISHES instead of counties. The 'domiciliary parent' is a unique Louisiana term for the parent with whom the child primarily resides in a joint custody arrangement.
